adrs.title: Use Vite + React for Management UI
adrs.summary: Uses Vite and React for the local management UI so it can reuse existing Frigg UI components and stay lightweight, with no Electron wrapper.

adrs.title: No Database for Local Development Tools
adrs.summary: The management GUI keeps no database or persistent storage; all state is runtime memory read from project files, so each session starts fresh.

adrs.title: Runtime State Only for Management GUI
adrs.summary: The management GUI uses a minimal local-only security model: no auth, no stored credentials, no encryption, localhost CORS, and read-only file access.

adrs.title: Project Structure Migration Tool
adrs.summary: Defines frigg migrate, a build-time CLI that rewrites an app's project structure from create-frigg-app to the frigg init layout while preserving custom code.

adrs.title: Admin Script Runner Service
adrs.summary: Adds an Admin Script Runner so adopters register admin operations in the app definition and run them sync or scheduled behind a dedicated admin key.

adrs.title: Integration Router v2 Restructuring
adrs.summary: Restructures the integration API into a v2 router with consistent naming, credential management, and proxy endpoints, dropping the duplicated modules routes.

adrs.title: Management UI Architecture
adrs.summary: The management UI runs as a separate Express server that proxies to running Frigg apps, keeping admin API keys off the browser across local and remote.

adrs.title: Frigg CLI Start Command Architecture
adrs.summary: frigg start runs pre-flight checks for Docker, the database, env files, and Prisma, offering to fix problems so local startup just works.

adrs.title: E2E Test Package Architecture
adrs.summary: Adds a self-contained e2e package that spins up a real Express server and in-memory MongoDB to test full integration lifecycles over HTTP.

adrs.title: Reporting as an Admin Operation
adrs.summary: Treats reporting as an admin operation so reports register in the app definition and run on the shared script-runner instead of a hardcoded core endpoint.

adrs.title: Integration Telemetry, Eventing & Feature-Usage Tracking
adrs.summary: Adopts OpenTelemetry as a vendor-neutral telemetry layer with auto-instrumentation and a durable per-integration usage store that feeds reports.

adrs.title: Database Schema Migrations
adrs.summary: Runs Prisma schema migrations from a VPC-internal Lambda triggered by CI/CD, tracking status in S3 so it needs no dependency on the tables it creates.

adrs.title: Integration Version Migrations
adrs.summary: Makes integration version migration a first-class admin operation that idempotently transforms persisted records, config, and mappings across versions.

adrs.title: One Numbered ADR Register
adrs.summary: Consolidates Frigg's two ADR sets into one numbered register under docs/architecture-decisions with a single structure, header, and index.

adrs.title: Extensions Taxonomy
adrs.summary: Defines Extensions as optional add-on code split into core, integration, and API-module types, distinct from required infrastructure Plugins.

adrs.title: Plugins
adrs.summary: Defines Plugins as swappable infrastructure packages (provider, database, encryption, queue, scheduler) so core depends on interfaces, not bundled deps.

adrs.title: Core Extensions
adrs.summary: Core Extensions add optional app-level functionality like alerting, monitoring, and a Slack admin bot, declared on appDefinition.extensions.

adrs.title: Integration Extensions
adrs.summary: Integration Extensions let an API module or shared library ship a bundle of routes, events, queues, and workers that an integration binds declaratively.

adrs.title: API Module Extensions
adrs.summary: API Module Extensions are the producer side: an API module exports reusable extension bundles under extensions.{name} with provider quirks built in.

adrs.title: Capabilities
adrs.summary: Capabilities are typed declarations on a Definition that name what a module, integration, or app can do and point at its spec and implementation.

adrs.title: Ontology
adrs.summary: The Ontology is layered, versioned context (universal, framework, vendor, instance) that compiles into an XML block agents see at session start.

adrs.title: Artifacts
adrs.summary: Artifacts are code or config an API module helps generate that runs outside Frigg on the provider's platform, with Frigg serving the runtime bridge.

adrs.title: Integration Templates
adrs.summary: Integration Templates are category base classes an adopter copies into their codebase, ShadCN-style, with sync and mapping pre-built and owned by them.

adrs.title: Global Entities
adrs.summary: Global Entities let integrations use shared app-owner service accounts instead of per-user credentials, and need the currently missing schema fields.

adrs.title: Agent Harness
adrs.summary: The Agent Harness is a package wiring ontology, capabilities, plugins, and templates into Claude Code's session so agents ground and validate Frigg work.

adrs.title: Evals
adrs.summary: Builds an 8-condition factorial eval to measure whether capabilities, ontology, and the harness each improve agent accuracy on Frigg tasks.

adrs.title: SSM Parameter Offload and Per-Function Environment Scoping
adrs.summary: Offloads large secrets to SSM and scopes env vars per function so Lambdas stay under the 4KB environment limit as the integration count grows.

adrs.title: Multi-Provider Support
adrs.summary: Introduces a provider plugin system so a single `provider` field switches the whole toolchain. Each provider ships as @friggframework/provider-{name} with adapters for deploy, config generation, queues, scheduling, secrets and handlers; Netlify is the first non-AWS target.

adrs.title: Decouple AWS SDK Dependencies from @friggframework/core
adrs.summary: Extracts every AWS SDK dependency out of @friggframework/core into @friggframework/provider-aws, wiring adapters explicitly at the composition root. Breaking change; it is what lets a non-AWS bundle contain no AWS SDK code.

adrs.title: Integration Versioning
adrs.summary: Opens the integration version contract — how versions are declared, compared, gated and made compatible — which ADR-013's record migrations key off. Exploratory: the decision is deliberately deferred pending research.

adrs.title: Concurrent OAuth Credential Refresh Across Lambda Invocations
adrs.summary: Deconflicts concurrent OAuth refreshes across Lambda invocations: a reactive database check before refresh and on 401 (adopt the winner's tokens, escalate only on proof of death), plus proactive scheduled refresh via admin scripts, and a fix for the silent SQS ack that hid the losses.

adrs.title: Integration Deletion Data Cleanup
adrs.summary: Defines what must be cleaned up when an integration is deleted — which records cascade, which are retained for audit, and which admin operation performs the sweep.

adrs.title: Aurora Serverless v2 scale-to-zero + NAT-free Lambda connectivity
adrs.summary: Runs Aurora Serverless v2 with scale-to-zero and reaches it from Lambda without a NAT gateway, cutting idle database and egress cost for low-traffic Frigg apps.

adrs.title: API-Key Login Auth Mode
adrs.summary: Adds an API-key login auth mode validated by the API module, so an integration can authenticate with a key rather than an OAuth round-trip.

adrs.title: App Init
adrs.summary: Defines what app init seeds into an adopter app — agent directories, ontology seed and conventions — as a starting point adopters grow over time.

adrs.title: Skills
adrs.summary: Ships .claude/skills/ alongside .claude/agents/ as the declarative, read-on-demand surface of knowledge, contracts and runbooks an agent loads explicitly when relevant.

adrs.title: Agent Pipeline
adrs.summary: Describes the agent pipeline that composes app init, skills, capabilities and ontology into a repeatable run.

adrs.title: Configuration & Secrets — Model & Tiers
adrs.summary: Establishes the configuration and secrets model and its tiers, separating framework config, app config and per-connection credentials, and where each physically lives.

adrs.title: Secrets & Config Provider Plugin
adrs.summary: Extends the ADR-016 plugin taxonomy with a secrets/config provider plugin: one typed core port, many adapters, so a new backing store needs no core change.

adrs.title: Variable & Secret Management — Admin API, CLI, GUI
adrs.summary: Adds the admin API, CLI and GUI surface for managing variables and secrets across all tiers, reusing the admin API key from ADR-010.

adrs.title: Configuration & Secrets — Docs & Adopter Maturation
adrs.summary: Covers how the configuration and secrets work is documented for adopters, and the maturation path a Frigg app follows from local env files to a managed store.
